# Command line reference

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-docs.sh from the help of every command; do not edit. -->

This page reproduces the help of every `dotsteward` command. To change it,
edit the help text in `cli/commands/` and run `tools/gen-docs.sh`.

## Entry points

| Where | How to run a command |
| --- | --- |
| In an instance | `./.dotsteward/cli.sh <command>`: the CLI pinned by the instance's `flake.lock`, built once per lock and cached. The wrappers `./rebuild.sh` and `./rollback.sh` call it for you. |
| Anywhere with Nix | `nix run github:arda-tuz/dotsteward -- <command>`: the newest release. Inside an instance prefer the pinned launcher. |
| In a framework checkout | `./cli/dotsteward <command>` |

## Global options

```text
dotsteward [--instance DIR] <command> [ARG...]
dotsteward --help
```

- `--instance DIR`: the instance to act on. Without it the CLI uses
  `DOTSTEWARD_INSTANCE`, then the nearest `workstation.toml` above the
  working directory. `version`, `scan`, `init` and `--help` need no instance.
- `--help`: the list of commands with their summaries.
  `dotsteward <command> --help` prints the help reproduced below.

## Output

Progress lines go to standard output as `[dotsteward] ...`; warnings and
errors go to standard error as `[dotsteward] WARNING: ...` and
`[dotsteward] ERROR: ...`. The pins and settings engines keep their own
`[pins]` and `[local-maintained-files]` prefixes. With `--json` a command
prints exactly one JSON document on standard output. The exit status of
every command is listed in [exit-codes.md](exit-codes.md).

## Environment

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `DOTSTEWARD_INSTANCE` | The instance directory, like `--instance`. |
| `DOTSTEWARD_STATE_ROOT` | The root of the machine records, instead of `state.root`. |
| `DOTSTEWARD_NIX_MAX_JOBS`, `DOTSTEWARD_NIX_CORES` | The Nix parallelism of the gate, instead of `gate.nix_max_jobs` and `gate.nix_cores` or the values derived from the machine. |
| `DOTSTEWARD_MEMORY_MIB`, `DOTSTEWARD_CPU_COUNT` | The memory (MiB) and CPU count the derived Nix parallelism of the gate and of `contribute check` reads, instead of the machine's. |
| `DOTSTEWARD_CONTRIBUTE_NIX_MAX_JOBS`, `DOTSTEWARD_CONTRIBUTE_NIX_CORES` | The Nix parallelism of the framework check in `contribute check`, instead of the values derived from the machine. |
| `DOTSTEWARD_MIN_FREE_GB` | The free space the gate requires in `/nix/store`, instead of `gate.min_free_gib`. |
| `DOTSTEWARD_CACHE_URL` | The binary cache the gate probes, instead of `gate.cache_url`. |
| `DOTSTEWARD_FRAMEWORK_OVERRIDE` | The framework flake reference of `--framework-override`. |
| `DOTSTEWARD_E2E_JOBS` | How many parallel E2E hooks `dotsteward e2e` runs at a time, like `--jobs` (default 3). |
| `DOTSTEWARD_APT_UPDATE_TIMEOUT` | Seconds one `apt-get update` may take before it is stopped and tried once more (default 600). |
| `DOTSTEWARD_APT_BRIDGE_TIMEOUT` | Seconds the deb transaction lets one refresh of the local APT bridge take before it leaves the rest to the bridge's timer (default 1800). |
| `DOTSTEWARD_ASSUME_YES` | `1` answers installer and package manager confirmations; meant for CI runners only. |
| `DOTSTEWARD_CLI` | A CLI that `.dotsteward/cli.sh` runs instead of building the pinned one. |
| `DOTSTEWARD_MACHINE` | The name of this machine, instead of `machine.json` of the state root ([machines.md](machines.md)). |
| `DOTSTEWARD_MACHINE_REUSE` | `1`: this machine is the reinstall of the machine whose name it takes, like `host init --reuse`. |

## Commands

| Command | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`agents`](#agents) | Install or check the agent tools, the skill layout and the agents checks of a profile |
| [`apply`](#apply) | Finish a maintain transaction in one command: gate, commit, activate, E2E, publish |
| [`bootstrap`](#bootstrap) | Bootstrap stage 1 (run by ./bootstrap.sh once Nix is installed) |
| [`component`](#component) | Run a component hook with the hook environment |
| [`context`](#context) | Print the facts of the instance on this machine (--json for skills) |
| [`contribute`](#contribute) | Change the dotsteward framework itself: mode, setup, start, commit, check, trial, publish, release, upgrade |
| [`doctor`](#doctor) | Check the health of the instance on this machine (--redact to share) |
| [`e2e`](#e2e) | Verify this machine against the instance: the end-to-end checks of a profile |
| [`gate`](#gate) | Validate the candidate tree of a maintenance transaction (the gate) |
| [`generate`](#generate) | Regenerate the .dotsteward/ mirrors and the derived lock values |
| [`host`](#host) | Name this machine and bring its host file to the remote (init, publish, show, list, rename, producer, check, platform) |
| [`incoming`](#incoming) | Answer what other machines changed: install it here, ask later, or never on this machine |
| [`init`](#init) | Create a new instance from the framework template (--dir, --remote, --components) |
| [`install`](#install) | Run the system-install phase (deb transaction, phase hooks) or check every install method |
| [`login-shell`](#login-shell) | Set, migrate or check the stable login shell of the instance |
| [`maintain`](#maintain) | Open a maintain transaction (maintain begin), which dotsteward apply finishes |
| [`pins`](#pins) | Check, sync, research and move the pinned versions of the instance's lock files |
| [`preflight`](#preflight) | Read-only check of this machine against the instance fast path (exit 3: adaptive route) |
| [`probes`](#probes) | Run the version, presence and feature probes of a generation's manifest |
| [`rebuild`](#rebuild) | Build the instance's Home Manager generation for this machine and optionally switch to it |
| [`rollback`](#rollback) | Undo the instance's Home Manager setup (login shell, managed links, force-linked files) |
| [`scan`](#scan) | Scan files, the staged index or a commit range for secrets and private data |
| [`settings`](#settings) | Sync tracked application settings with the instance's settings buffer |
| [`skills`](#skills) | Track the user's own skills, and report what the instance means for this machine |
| [`state`](#state) | Record the state this machine observes on its own state branch, push it, fetch and show the state of every machine |
| [`static`](#static) | Check the static contracts of an instance or of the framework source |
| [`sync`](#sync) | Old name of generate: a warning, then generate with the same arguments (until 2.0.0) |
| [`txn`](#txn) | Prepare, publish and report a maintenance transaction |
| [`update`](#update) | Old name of txn: a warning, then txn with the same arguments (until 2.0.0) |
| [`upgrade`](#upgrade) | Bring this machine and the shared lock to the newest stable versions, with one command |
| [`version`](#version) | Print the framework version, source revision and narHash |

## `agents`

Install or check the agent tools, the skill layout and the agents checks of a profile.

```text
Usage: dotsteward agents install|check --profile PROFILE [--generation PATH]
                                        [--keep-going] [--json]
                                        [--skip-validation]

install makes the agent tools and the skill layout of PROFILE match the
instance: official-binary and pypi components, the canonical skill root
~/.agents/skills with its entries and link-root links, copies of missing
instance skills, refreshed drifted copies (backed up first), removed
dangling skill links and the agents hooks; then it validates. check runs
the same steps without changing anything and fails on the first
difference. A skill of the user's own (a repo-owned sentinel revision in the
lock) is never overwritten: install takes a newer copy of the repository only
when the local copy did not change, and a difference is a note for check,
never a failure; see `dotsteward skills status`.

  --profile PROFILE   a profile of the instance (required)
  --generation PATH   a built Home Manager generation: its manifest, its
                      framework skill sources and its home-path/bin first on
                      PATH for the validation; default: the active
                      generation, else the instance's manifest mirror
  --keep-going        record each failure and go on with the steps that do
                      not depend on it
  --json              print { "result": "passed|failed", "findings": [ {
                      "step", "path", "code", "message" } ] } on standard
                      output; logs go to standard error
  --skip-validation   install only: leave out the validation (commands,
                      floors, probes, checks.agents hooks), which `agents
                      check` (run by dotsteward e2e) does; rebuild --switch
                      installs this way

Exit status: 0 done or verified, 1 refusal or failed check, or the status
of a failed command.
```

## `apply`

Finish a maintain transaction in one command: gate, commit, activate, E2E, publish.

```text
usage: dotsteward apply [-h] [-m SUBJECT] [--activate | --no-activate]
                        [--publish | --no-publish] [--profile PROFILE]
                        [--json]

Finishes a maintain transaction in one command: stages every change of the
checkout, regenerates the mirrors, runs the gate in the maintain scope,
commits with SUBJECT and the trace line of this machine, then with --activate
installs the system-level components an adopt-mode profile needs, runs rebuild
--switch and E2E against the base, and with --publish runs txn publish; when
another machine published first, it moves the commits onto the new tip, proves
and activates them again and pushes again, three times at most. [maintain]
activate and publish of workstation.toml are the defaults (both false). Run
the same command again after a fix or a sudo step: it does what is left. Exit
status: 0 done, 1 a refusal or a red step, 2 usage error, 3 a sudo step or a
person waits (review.json: a change of the same lines here and on the remote,
or a remote that kept moving), 6 no network: the push waits, 130 interrupted.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -m, --message SUBJECT
                        the conventional commit subject
  --activate            activate here
  --no-activate         do not activate
  --publish             publish the commits
  --no-publish          keep the commits here
  --profile PROFILE     the profile to activate (default: this machine's)
  --json                print the report on standard output
```

## `bootstrap`

Bootstrap stage 1 (run by ./bootstrap.sh once Nix is installed).

```text
Usage: dotsteward bootstrap --profile PROFILE --stage 1

Stage 1 of a fresh-machine bootstrap, run by the instance's ./bootstrap.sh
(stage 0) once Nix is installed: the name of this machine, the
system-install phase, rebuild --switch, the login shell, the desktop apply
hooks (fresh mode), the E2E checks and the host file of this machine. Start a
bootstrap with ./bootstrap.sh --profile PROFILE.

  --profile PROFILE   the instance's bootstrap profile (profiles.bootstrap)
  --stage 1           the stage to run (internal; stage 0 is ./bootstrap.sh)

Exit status: 0 done, 1 refusal, else the status of the failing step (3:
the adaptive route).
```

## `component`

Run a component hook with the hook environment.

```text
Usage: dotsteward component run NAME HOOK [--profile PROFILE]
                                [--generation PATH] [-- ARG...]

Runs hook HOOK of component NAME with the hook environment and the
arguments after --. The hook is looked up in every hook list of the
manifest (hooks.*, checks.e2e, checks.agents).

  --profile PROFILE   DOTSTEWARD_PROFILE of the hook; default: the current
                      profile recorded by the last rebuild, else
                      profiles.check
  --generation PATH   a built Home Manager generation whose manifest (and
                      hook scripts) to use; default: the active generation,
                      else the instance's manifest mirror

The component must be enabled and active in the profile.

Exit status: the hook's; 1 for a refusal.
```

## `context`

Print the facts of the instance on this machine (--json for skills).

```text
Usage: dotsteward context [--json]

Prints the facts of the instance on this machine: the instance,
the check and runtime identity, the state record paths, profiles, gate
parameters, commit rules, protected paths, skill overlays, components with
their methods, settings targets and commands, the settings buffer's target
names and entry ids (never values), the instance skills, the framework and
its upstream, and the platform.

  --json      one JSON document (schema/context.schema.json) on stdout;
              without it, one "[dotsteward] key: value" line per fact
  -h, --help  this help

The instance comes from --instance, DOTSTEWARD_INSTANCE or the nearest
workstation.toml above the working directory. Exit 0, or 1 for a usage
error, an invalid configuration or an unreadable source.
```

## `contribute`

Change the dotsteward framework itself: mode, setup, start, commit, check, trial, publish, release, upgrade.

```text
Usage: dotsteward [--instance DIR] contribute <step> [OPTION...]
       dotsteward contribute --help

Runs one step of a framework contribution from this machine:
reproduce, fix generically, test here, then publish to the upstream
(owner mode) or to the user's fork (fork mode) and upgrade the instance.
The framework upstream is the dotsteward input of the instance flake.lock;
[upstream] in workstation.toml chooses the mode, the fork and the local
clone. The dotsteward-contribute skill drives the steps in order.

Steps:
  mode [--json]           owner or fork, and why: owner needs
                          upstream.contribute = "owner", a gh login, push
                          permission on the upstream and a local clone
                          whose origin is the upstream (or no clone yet);
                          otherwise fork mode, with a warning (never an
                          error). --json: {schema_version, mode,
                          configured, fallback, upstream, upstream_url,
                          upstream_remote, fork, fork_url, clone,
                          gh_login}. Writes nothing.
  setup [--create-fork]   clones upstream.local_clone (owner: the
                          upstream; fork: the fork, plus an `upstream`
                          remote) or fetches an existing clone, and sets
                          its user.name and user.email (the GitHub login
                          and noreply address) and core.hooksPath
                          (.githooks: the clone's pre-commit, commit-msg
                          and pre-push hooks). A missing fork is created
                          with `gh repo fork --clone=false` only with
                          --create-fork (or DOTSTEWARD_ASSUME_YES=1).
                          Owner mode refuses without the denylist; fork
                          mode warns.
  start --slug SLUG [--promote NAME]
                          branch fix/SLUG from a freshly fetched upstream
                          main and a new run (the current one); the same
                          SLUG again resumes its unfinished run. --promote:
                          the run moves the private component NAME (source
                          "instance") into the catalog, with the user's
                          explicit approval; recorded as promote, it
                          exempts exactly the term NAME from the
                          instance-leak scan of the run's check (the same
                          SLUG again sets it on the unfinished run;
                          another NAME is refused)
  commit -m SUBJECT [-m PARAGRAPH...] [--test]
                          in the run's clone: stages everything (git add
                          -A) and commits with the clone's identity (from
                          setup) and UTC dates, whatever the environment
                          says. SUBJECT is a conventional commit subject
                          (TYPE(AREA): text, TYPE from
                          commit.conventional_types of `dotsteward
                          context --json`); further -m options are the
                          paragraphs of the body; trailers and attribution
                          lines (Co-Authored-By, Signed-off-by,
                          Claude-Session) are refused, as the clone's
                          commit-msg and pre-commit hooks refuse them and
                          non-UTC dates for a plain git commit. --test: the
                          reproduction test (a test subject). Refused
                          before the reproduction failed and after
                          publish; a commit after a passing check sends
                          the run back to check
  check [--expect-fail PATH]
                          with --expect-fail: runs `tests/run.sh PATH` in
                          the clone, which must fail (the reproduction).
                          Without it, the framework gate on a clean clone
                          at the run's branch: the privacy scans (tree;
                          commits after upstream main with metadata rules
                          and the denylist; the instance-leak scan with
                          terms from `dotsteward context --json`), then
                          `nix flake check` with the framework check's own
                          parallelism (derived from the machine, at most 4
                          jobs; DOTSTEWARD_CONTRIBUTE_NIX_MAX_JOBS and
                          DOTSTEWARD_CONTRIBUTE_NIX_CORES override it).
                          Records test_sha and tested_tree on success; any
                          failure before publish withdraws an earlier pass
                          (the run goes back to check); a privacy stop or
                          a failed nix flake check after a trial switch
                          also runs the recovery (see abort). A branch that
                          changes privacy/allowlist.txt or
                          privacy/policy.toml is a privacy hard stop: they
                          change only in their own, manually reviewed
                          pull request; the leak terms skip only the
                          allowlist of upstream main. A branch without
                          commits after upstream main is refused, except
                          after a tree mismatch
  trial [--build-only]    the trial on this machine: gate,
                          rebuild --switch and e2e of the instance with
                          --framework-override git+file://<clone>?rev=<the
                          checked commit>, run by the candidate's own CLI
                          (the instance's dotsteward package built with
                          that override); --build-only: gate and rebuild
                          --build-only (no switch, no e2e). Red: nothing is
                          published and a trial switch is recovered. An
                          instance HEAD ahead of origin (commits that wait
                          for the fix): e2e, and the recovery's, checks
                          the remote against origin's commit
                          (--expected-remote-base)
  publish [--pr-to-upstream]
                          owner: push fix/SLUG, open (or reuse) the pull
                          request, wait for its lint and privacy checks
                          only (lint of ci.yml, generic of privacy.yml;
                          the full check runs on main after the merge; a
                          build-only trial also needs clean-install.yml
                          green on the commit, dispatched on the branch
                          when missing),
                          merge by fast-forwarding main to the checked
                          commit (never a merge made by GitHub) and
                          verify the merged tree is the tested tree; fork:
                          push, the fork's CI, fast-forward the fork's
                          main, an upstream pull request only with
                          upstream.pr_to_upstream or --pr-to-upstream.
                          VERSION of the checked commit must be the
                          release its commits are based on (the run
                          releases nothing: release trains) or exactly the
                          next release (a release commit, tools/version.sh
                          bump), before anything is pushed and again
                          before the merge. Upstream main moved: the
                          branch is rebased and the run goes back to check
                          (exit 5); so does a tree mismatch after the
                          merge, with the branch on the merged main. A git
                          read or push that fails for the network is made
                          again (a push reads its ref first), a push that
                          the remote or a hook refused never
  release [--major]       the release that VERSION of the merged commit
                          names, when it is the next one: after the newest
                          v* tag, as the conventional commits since the
                          release they are based on decide (any feat: the
                          next minor, else the next patch; from 0.0.0
                          without a tag; a breaking change: the next
                          major, cut only with --major). Nothing pending
                          (VERSION still the base release) is refused:
                          report ends the run at publish. An annotated
                          tag on the merged commit, pushed once main's CI
                          (ci.yml with the full check, privacy.yml) is
                          green on that commit, waited for as publish
                          waits; owner: gh release create --notes-file
                          (the commits since the previous release under
                          Features, Fixes and Other) --verify-tag. A
                          release tag already on the merged commit (cut by
                          release.yml first, also while release waits for
                          main's CI or before its push) is recorded as the
                          run's release once main's CI is green, its
                          GitHub release created when missing; a tag
                          elsewhere is red with nothing changed. A red
                          release keeps a trial switch (the change is
                          merged with the tested tree): no recovery
  upgrade [--tag TAG | --main] [--carry] [--build-only]
                          the instance to the release: update prepare
                          --scope maintain, the dotsteward input of
                          flake.nix, nix flake update dotsteward,
                          bootstrap.sh and .dotsteward/cli.sh from the
                          release's template/, sync, gate, a commit with
                          commit.upgrade_subject ({version}: TAG without
                          v), rebuild --switch and e2e (--build-only:
                          rebuild --build-only), update publish --scope
                          maintain; re-runnable. --main (right after
                          publish too): the merged commit instead, the
                          one check and trial passed for, pinned by its
                          revision on the same repository URL
                          ({version}: main@<12-digit commit>). An instance
                          whose HEAD has commits that origin lacks is
                          refused; --carry saves them, resets the instance
                          to origin, upgrades, applies them again on top
                          (a conflict outside the generated mirrors stops
                          with the cherry-pick in progress: resolve it,
                          git cherry-pick --continue, then upgrade again),
                          syncs and gates the whole tree, and publishes
                          them with the upgrade. A red upgrade keeps a
                          trial switch, as a red release does: run it again
                          once the cause is fixed
  abort                   ends the run; after a trial switch it first runs
                          the recovery: rebuild --switch and e2e without
                          an override, back to the pinned framework
  report [--json]         the run's result (outcome, pull request, merged
                          commit, release, instance commit, tests, the
                          promoted component); ends the run with the
                          outcome completed, or at step release with the
                          outcome published (a run that ends at publish,
                          without a release tag or an instance commit, once
                          the recovery of a trial switch passed; refused
                          after upgrade --main started)
  status [--json] [--wait [--timeout SECONDS]]
                          the run's state and its running step (--json: the
                          state document); once merged_sha is set also
                          main_ci, main's CI for the merged commit read
                          now: {sha, state (pending, green, red or
                          unknown), url, runs}. --wait: first waits until
                          no step of the run runs (at most SECONDS), then
                          exits with the status of the run's last step (0,
                          1, 4 or 5; 1 for an interrupted step or an
                          unknown outcome; 0 before the first step), or 3
                          when SECONDS passed first
Options of the steps that use a run (commit, check, status, remote steps):
  --id ID                 that run instead of the current one

Running steps: check, trial, publish, release, upgrade, abort and report
record running = {step, pid, started_at} in the run's state while they
work and replace it with last_step = {step, status, started_at, ended_at}
when they end, also after a failure and on SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP.
While a step of any run is running, setup, start, commit and those steps
refuse and name it. A marker whose process is gone (killed, or the machine
stopped) is stale: status and the next step report and clear it, and its
outcome is unknown (last_step.status null).

State: one file per run, <state root>/contribute/<id>.json (0600, in a 0700
directory), id = <UTC timestamp>-<slug>, with the fields id, slug, mode,
clone, branch, base_sha, test_sha, tested_tree, trial_switched, pr,
merged_sha, tag, instance_commit and step, plus profile, trial, trial_sha,
upgrade, upgrade_to, instance_base, upgrade_commit, carry, recovery and
outcome from the remote steps (see cli/lib/contribute-remote.sh), running
and last_step (see Running steps) and promote (start --promote, only when
given); <state root>/contribute/current holds the current run's id. step
is the next step of the run: reproduce, fix, check, trial, publish,
release, upgrade, report or done; every step reads and updates the file,
so an interrupted run resumes at step.

Privacy: the denylist is ~/.config/dotsteward/denylist.txt, the file the
pre-push hook reads; check needs it in both modes. Findings are always
redacted. Instance-leak terms are skipped when they are shorter than 4
characters, equal to a line of the clone's privacy/allowlist.txt (the
scanner masks those strings), part of the contributor's public identity
(the clone's user.name and user.email, carried by every commit) or already
in the content of the fetched upstream main outside the allowlisted
strings (published before, so no new leak); the run's promote (start
--promote) is exempt as well, as the one term the run exists to publish,
never through privacy/allowlist.txt or privacy/policy.toml. Any finding (or
scan failure) is a hard stop: exit 4, nothing may be published.

Exit status:
  0  done
  1  refused or failed
  3  still running (status --wait --timeout): the step has not ended yet;
     wait again
  4  privacy hard stop (check): nothing may be published
  5  back to check (publish): upstream main moved, the branch was rebased
     (or must be rebased by hand after a conflict)
```

## `doctor`

Check the health of the instance on this machine (--redact to share).

```text
Usage: dotsteward doctor [--json] [--redact]

Checks the health of the instance on this machine, read-only: the
configuration, the runtime identity, Nix, the launcher cache, the .dotsteward
mirrors, the last built generation's manifest and the age of the gate memo.
Each check is ok, warn, fail or skip.

  --json      one JSON document on stdout: the checks and the context
              (`dotsteward context --json`); without it, a line per check
  --redact    replace home directories, usernames, the hostname, the remote
              and private names (settings entries and targets, instance
              components and skills, values quoted by configuration
              problems) with <redacted>, to share the report
  -h, --help  this help

Exit 0, or 1 when a check fails or for a usage error.
```

## `e2e`

Verify this machine against the instance: the end-to-end checks of a profile.

```text
Usage: dotsteward e2e --profile PROFILE [--expected-remote-base OID]
                      [--framework-override REF] [--generation PATH]
                      [--jobs N] [--keep-going] [--json] [--list]
                      [--skip-repo-checks]

Verifies that this machine matches the instance for PROFILE after a
rebuild: commands, component E2E hooks, managed links, agent rules, files,
the agents check, tracked settings, the login shell, the instance checkout
and its remote, and the framework skills of the generation.

  --profile PROFILE          a profile of the instance (required)
  --expected-remote-base OID before a publish: the remote branch must still
                             be OID (40 hex digits) and OID an ancestor of
                             HEAD, instead of HEAD itself
  --framework-override REF   the framework flake reference the generation
                             was built with (also DOTSTEWARD_FRAMEWORK_OVERRIDE);
                             reported with the run
  --generation PATH          a built Home Manager generation: its manifest,
                             its framework skills and its home-path/bin
                             first on PATH; default: the active generation,
                             else the instance's manifest mirror
  --jobs N                   run at most N parallel hooks (parallel: true in
                             the manifest) at a time (default:
                             DOTSTEWARD_E2E_JOBS, else 3); 1 runs every hook
                             alone, in the foreground
  --keep-going               run every check and record each failure
  --json                     print { "result": "passed|failed", "findings":
                             [ { "step", "path", "code", "message" } ] } on
                             standard output (step is the check id); logs
                             go to standard error
  --list                     print the check ids of PROFILE in run order and
                             run nothing (with --json: { "profile", "checks" })
  --skip-repo-checks         skip the instance checkout and remote checks
                             (CI fixtures only)

Exit status: 0 every check passed (or --list), 1 a refusal or a failed
check.
```

## `gate`

Validate the candidate tree of a maintenance transaction (the gate).

```text
Usage: dotsteward [--instance DIR] gate [--scope update|maintain] [--force]
                  [--expected-base OID] [--framework-override REF]

Proves the tree that `git add -A && git commit` would record in the
instance clone, without committing, pushing or activating anything. Order:
the arguments; the clone (top of a git work tree, on instance.branch,
origin exactly instance.remote); the lock <state>/update/validate.lock (a
running gate is refused at once); untracked files (refused, Nix does not
see them); the base OID; in the update scope the allowlist of changed
paths; the candidate tree id; the writer classes (on a machine that is not
the producer of the base, no pin of the base moves, and no machine writes
the host file of another: `writer-class` lines, docs/machines.md); `nix
--version`; the memo; then five quiet
steps, each with its output in <state>/update/validate.log:
  preflight    the binary cache answers (gate.cache_url) and /nix/store
               has gate.min_free_gib GiB free; never fall back to mirrors
  static       the static checks that need this machine: dotsteward
               static --only scripts (the [gate] static scripts with
               DOTSTEWARD_SANDBOX=0, so their parts outside the sandbox
               run), with --only privacy first when [privacy] names a
               denylist (a file outside the instance, which the sandbox
               never reads); every other static check runs once, in the
               sandbox, in checks.<system>.instance-contract of the flake
               check
  pins         dotsteward pins check --nix
  flake-check  nix flake check with gate.nix_max_jobs and gate.nix_cores
               (derived from the memory and CPUs of the machine when
               workstation.toml sets none; see `dotsteward context --json`)
  cli-probes   nix build checks.<primary system>.home, then dotsteward
               probes --generation <built path>
and records <state>/update/validation.json and the hand-off
<state>/update/generation.json. Every Nix call keeps the lock file as it
is (--no-update-lock-file).

Options:
  --scope S          update (default): every path changed since the base
                     must match the update allowlist (framework defaults,
                     the component paths of .dotsteward/manifest.*.json,
                     gate.update_allowlist) and the settings buffer never
                     changes; maintain: no path restriction
  --force            ignore the memo (every other check still runs)
  --expected-base OID
                     the base OID; default: base_oid of candidate.json
                     when it was prepared for this instance, else
                     `git merge-base HEAD origin/<branch>`, else, in a
                     clone whose branch was never pushed (no
                     origin/<branch>, as right after `dotsteward init`),
                     HEAD, so the first tree is validated before the
                     first push
  --framework-override REF
                     evaluate the instance with its dotsteward input
                     replaced by the flake reference REF, in memory
                     (--override-input dotsteward REF
                     --no-write-lock-file); the steps see
                     DOTSTEWARD_FRAMEWORK_OVERRIDE=REF, and the instance
                     contract checks bootstrap.sh and .dotsteward/cli.sh
                     as the upgrade to REF writes them (from its
                     template/; the checkout is not changed). Default:
                     the DOTSTEWARD_FRAMEWORK_OVERRIDE environment variable

Memo: a passed record answers without running a step when the tree id,
`nix --version`, the gate version (the framework VERSION), the framework
override, the sha256 of the configured privacy denylist and the scope all
equal the record's (txn publish takes a record of its own scope only); the
root is not part of the key. A memo answer for another base records that
base, which the writer classes and the update allowlist were checked
against first; txn publish takes a record of its own base only. A failed
run keeps the previous record.

validation.json (schema_version "1.1"): result, tree_oid, base_oid, scope,
nix_version, gate_version, framework_override (or null), denylist_sha256
(or null), root, validated_at, total_seconds, step_seconds (preflight,
static, pins, flake-check, cli-probes), log.

generation.json (schema_version "1.0"), the hand-off to `dotsteward
rebuild`: tree_oid, profile (profiles.check), system (the primary
system), username and home (the check identity: identity.username and
identity.home, identity.darwin_home on darwin), generation (the store path
the cli-probes step built and probed), framework_override (or null), root
and recorded_at. rebuild activates that generation instead of evaluating
and building again when the tree of HEAD, its profile and system, $USER,
$HOME, its framework override and its checkout are the same; a memo
answer and a failed run keep the previous record.

Output: one "ok" line per step, then one JSON line {result, tree_oid,
scope, total_seconds, step_seconds}; a memo answer prints {result,
tree_oid, scope, validated_at, total_seconds, memo: true}. A failed step
prints its FAILED line and the last 60 log lines on stderr.

Exit status: 0 passed (or answered from the memo), 1 refused or failed.
```

## `generate`

Regenerate the .dotsteward/ mirrors and the derived lock values.

```text
Usage: dotsteward generate [--nix] [--skill NAME]...

Evaluates the instance's dotstewardMirrors output (`nix eval --json
--no-update-lock-file <instance>#dotstewardMirrors`), writes every mirror
that changed to .dotsteward/<name> byte for byte (atomically), removes
manifest.*.json and stage0.*.env mirrors the evaluation no longer
produces, then runs `dotsteward pins sync` with the same flags against the
fresh mirrors. Untracked, not ignored files other than those mirrors are
refused before any Nix call, because Nix does not see them. Exit codes:
0 ok, 1 refusal or error, else the status of `pins sync`.
```

## `host`

Name this machine and bring its host file to the remote (init, publish, show, list, rename, producer, check, platform).

```text
usage: dotsteward host [-h] SUBCOMMAND ...

The name of this machine and its host file hosts/<name>.toml.

positional arguments:
  SUBCOMMAND
    init      name this machine
    publish   bring hosts/<name>.toml to the remote
    show      print this machine
    list      print the machines of this checkout
    rename    give this machine another name
    producer  name the machine that moves the upstream values
    check     check the host files and the machines lists of the tree
    platform  print the platform of this machine and what its platform files
              say

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

Exit status: 0 done, 1 refusal, 2 usage error; host publish: 4 a privacy
finding, 6 no network or no login. Both publish nothing, and 6 asks to run it
again.
```

### `host init`

```text
usage: dotsteward host init [-h] [--name NAME] [--profile PROFILE]
                            [--tags TAG,TAG] [--reuse]

Names this machine. Without a name on the command line it asks on a terminal;
without a terminal the name comes from DOTSTEWARD_MACHINE, or with
DOTSTEWARD_ASSUME_YES=1 from the cleaned host name, else it is a usage error.
A name in hosts/ is the name of another machine, or of this one before a
reinstall: a terminal asks, without a terminal it takes --reuse or
DOTSTEWARD_MACHINE_REUSE=1. Only <state>/machine.json is written; the checkout
stays as it is.

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --name NAME        the name of this machine: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$
  --profile PROFILE  the profile this machine runs (default: the one of its
                     last rebuild, never a default of the instance)
  --tags TAG,TAG     the tags of this machine
  --reuse            this machine is the reinstall of a machine whose name is
                     in hosts/
```

### `host publish`

```text
usage: dotsteward host publish [-h]

Writes hosts/<name>.toml on the remote branch in one commit without force, and
leaves the checkout as it is. The other keys of the file stay. Without a
network or a login it exits 6 and nothing is lost: it works out the same again
next time.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

```text
usage: dotsteward host show [-h] [--json]

Prints this machine.

```

```text
usage: dotsteward host list [-h] [--json]

Prints the machines hosts/ of this checkout registers.

options:

  --json      print one JSON document
```

```text
usage: dotsteward host rename [-h] NEW

Gives this machine another name: its host file, the machines lists that name

positional arguments:
```

```text
Publish that commit like any maintain commit.
```

```text
usage: dotsteward host check [-h]

Checks every hosts/<name>.toml against schema/host.schema.json and nix.systems
and profiles.names, and every machines list of the skills lock and of the
plugin tables: not empty, and only names in hosts/; every
platforms/<platform>.toml against schema/platform.schema.json, and a fast path
```

```text
usage: dotsteward host platform [-h] [--json]

Prints the platform of this machine (ubuntu-24.04, macos-15), its layers from
the most specific one (the release, the operating system, linux or darwin),
the files of platforms/ that exist for them and what they say about
components, each from the most specific layer: a component that is unavailable
here is left out by every command (skills effective names the reason
platform).

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print one JSON document
```

## `incoming`

Answer what other machines changed: install it here, ask later, or never on this machine.

```text
usage: dotsteward incoming [-h] [--json] SUBCOMMAND ...

What other machines changed. The repository moves forward by itself; a new or
changed skill, plugin or component lands on this machine only when the answer
says so: install, ask later, or never on this machine. Without a subcommand:
brings the checkout forward and asks, one item at a time; without a terminal
every item is ask later, review.json holds the questions and the exit status
is 3.

positional arguments:
  SUBCOMMAND
    list      what waits, without a fetch
    show      what an item is about
    answer    answer one item

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print one JSON document

Exit status: 0 done, 1 refusal, 2 usage error, 3 questions wait and no
terminal can answer them.
```

### `incoming list`

```text
usage: dotsteward incoming list [-h] [--json]

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

```text
positional arguments:

options:
```

```text
usage: dotsteward incoming answer [-h] (--install | --never) [--json] ID

--install installs a skill or a plugin at once, removes what the repository no
longer holds for this machine, and leaves a component to the next upgrade or

this machine. To ask later, do nothing.

positional arguments:
  ID

options:

  --never     never on this machine
```

## `init`

Create a new instance from the framework template (--dir, --remote, --components).

```text
usage: dotsteward init --dir DIR --remote URL [OPTION]...

Create a dotsteward instance from the framework template in DIR (missing,
empty, or filled by `nix flake init -t`), lock it, generate its mirrors, check
its pins and commit it. All or nothing: on a refusal or a failed step DIR is
left as it was.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR             the instance directory
  --remote URL          instance.remote: exactly what `git remote get-url
                        origin` will print
  --username U          check identity user name (default: $USER)
  --home H              check identity home directory (default: $HOME)
  --name N              instance.name (default: the name of DIR)
  --checkout PATH       instance.checkout, the canonical clone (default: DIR,
                        as ~/... when it is below $HOME)
  --components LIST     comma-separated catalog components to enable (default:
                        none)
  --method COMPONENT=METHOD
                        the install method of a chosen component (repeatable)
  --method-platform COMPONENT=linux:METHOD,darwin:METHOD
                        per-platform install methods of a chosen component
                        (repeatable)
  --systems LIST        nix.systems, the first one primary (from x86_64-linux,
                        aarch64-darwin; default: x86_64-linux)
  --profiles ADOPT_NAME,FRESH_NAME
                        the adopt profile (default and check) and the fresh
                        profile (bootstrap) (default: workstation,fresh)
  --allow-unfree        nix.allow_unfree = true
  --contribute {fork,owner}
                        upstream.contribute (default: fork)
  --framework-ref vX.Y.Z
                        the framework release tag the dotsteward input pins
  --framework-url URL   the whole flake reference of the dotsteward input
  --machine NAME        hosts.producer: the machine that moves the values that
                        come from upstream, usually this one
  --no-git              neither initialize git nor commit
  --non-interactive     never prompt (init never prompts; accepted for
                        scripts)
  --json                print the result as one JSON document

Exit status: 0 success, 1 refusal or failed step, 2 usage error.
```

## `install`

Run the system-install phase (deb transaction, phase hooks) or check every install method.

```text
Usage: dotsteward install --profile PROFILE [--component NAME]... [--check-only] [--json] [--generation PATH]

Runs the system-install phase of PROFILE: in fresh mode the preflight gate,
one apt transaction for the deb components (DEBs below their floor are
downloaded and verified first; -y only with DOTSTEWARD_ASSUME_YES=1), the
floors verified afterwards, then the systemInstall, postInstall and forbid
hooks. When a hook to run is a Nix store path of the manifest mirror, the
generation is built first (dotsteward rebuild --build-only, after the
preflight gate) and its manifest is used. In adopt mode the phase is
skipped, unless components are named.

  --profile PROFILE   a profile of the instance (required)
  --component NAME    only this active component and its hooks (repeatable);
                      in adopt mode the phase runs for the named components
                      as in fresh mode, and --check-only checks them by their
                      method
  --check-only        check every active component by its method, run only
                      the forbid hooks (store-path hooks from the active
                      generation); no change, no preflight
  --json              print the report as one JSON document on standard
                      output; logs go to standard error
  --generation PATH   read the manifest of a built generation (its hook
                      scripts are store paths) instead of the instance's
                      .dotsteward/manifest.<system>.json mirror

Exit status: 0 done or satisfied, 1 refusal or failed check, the
preflight's status (3: adaptive route) when it stops the phase.
```

## `login-shell`

Set, migrate or check the stable login shell of the instance.

```text
Usage: dotsteward login-shell set|migrate|check --profile PROFILE
                              [--generation PATH]

set makes the instance's login shell (the manifest's login_shell) the login
shell of the user, adding it to the shells file first. migrate moves a
versioned Nix zsh login shell to that stable path and only warns when sudo
would need a password and there is no terminal. check verifies that the
shell is executable, listed in the shells file and the user's login shell.

  --profile PROFILE   a profile of the instance (required)
  --generation PATH   a built Home Manager generation whose manifest names
                      the login shell; default: the active generation, else
                      the instance's manifest mirror

Exit status: 0 done or verified, 1 refusal or failed check, or the status
of a failed system command.
```

## `maintain`

Open a maintain transaction (maintain begin), which dotsteward apply finishes.

```text
usage: dotsteward maintain [-h] begin ...

Opens a maintain transaction: checks that this is the instance checkout on its
branch, fast-forwards it when it is only behind the remote, runs the read-only
preflight of the profile, records the base with txn prepare in the maintain
scope and reads the settings status. Exit status: 0 open, 1 refused, 2 usage
error, 3 open with questions for the user, or the adaptive route (nothing
opened), 6 no network (nothing opened).

positional arguments:
  begin
    begin     open a maintain transaction

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

```text
usage: dotsteward maintain begin [-h] [--profile PROFILE] [--json]

Opens a maintain transaction: checks that this is the instance checkout on its
branch, fast-forwards it when it is only behind the remote, runs the read-only
preflight of the profile, records the base with txn prepare in the maintain
scope and reads the settings status. Exit status: 0 open, 1 refused, 2 usage
error, 3 open with questions for the user, or the adaptive route (nothing
opened), 6 no network (nothing opened).

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --profile PROFILE  the profile of the preflight (default: this machine's)
  --json             print one JSON document on standard output
```

## `preflight`

Read-only check of this machine against the instance fast path (exit 3: adaptive route).

```text
Usage: dotsteward preflight --read-only [--json] [--profile PROFILE]

Read-only checks of this machine against the instance's fast path, from
the stage-0 mirror .dotsteward/stage0.<platform>.env: the operating
system, architecture and desktop, the preflight detectors of the enabled
components, the Nix version, the free space of $HOME and whether the
instance remote answers. Nothing is written.

  --read-only         required
  --json              print the facts as one JSON document
  --profile PROFILE   a profile of the instance (default: profiles.bootstrap)

Exit status: 0 on the fast route, 3 on the adaptive route (after a
warning), 1 for a refusal.
```

## `probes`

Run the version, presence and feature probes of a generation's manifest.

```text
Usage: dotsteward probes (--generation PATH | --manifest FILE --path-prefix DIR)

Runs the probe registry of the instance's check profile
(profiles.check, the profile of checks.<system>.home that the gate builds):
  --generation PATH   a built generation: its manifest
                      PATH/home-path/share/dotsteward/manifest.json, its
                      commands from PATH/home-path/bin
  --manifest FILE     a manifest file, with
  --path-prefix DIR   the directory searched first for the probe commands
The prefix applies to the probe commands only. Expected versions come from
the instance's lock files (pins.versions_lock and skills.lock), so the
command needs the instance (--instance, DOTSTEWARD_INSTANCE or the working
directory). Exit 0 when every probe passes, 1 on the first failure or an
invalid manifest or argument.
```

## `rebuild`

Build the instance's Home Manager generation for this machine and optionally switch to it.

```text
Usage: dotsteward rebuild --profile PROFILE --switch|--build-only
                          [--framework-override REF]

Builds the Home Manager generation of PROFILE for the running user and home
through the machine's host flake (<state>/host-overrides), or reuses the
generation a passing gate built for the same tree, profile, user, home
and framework override (<state>/update/generation.json). --build-only
stops after the build and changes nothing outside the state directory.
--switch then runs the preActivate hooks, adopts the declared files,
activates the generation, applies the tracked settings, installs the agent
tools and moves a versioned login shell to the stable path. The agent
tools are installed without their validation: `dotsteward e2e` checks
them, so run it after the rebuild.

  --profile PROFILE          a profile of the instance (required)
  --switch                   activate the built generation
  --build-only               build only (with --switch, --switch wins)
  --framework-override REF   build with the framework at the flake
                             reference REF instead of the locked one,
                             without writing a lock file (default:
                             DOTSTEWARD_FRAMEWORK_OVERRIDE)

The instance must be the root of a git repository without uncommitted
changes or untracked files.

Exit status: 0 done, 1 refusal, or the status of a failed step.
```

## `rollback`

Undo the instance's Home Manager setup (login shell, managed links, force-linked files).

```text
Usage: dotsteward rollback --latest --dry-run [--json]
       dotsteward rollback --latest --apply

Undoes the instance's Home Manager setup: restores the platform default
login shell, removes the shells-file line this system added, removes the
managed links (no Home Manager before the first install) or activates the
recorded previous Home Manager generation, and restores the force-linked
files from their backups. Settings files, Nix, the packages and user data
stay.

  --latest    roll back to the state before the first install (required)
  --dry-run   print the plan and change nothing
  --json      with --dry-run: print the plan as JSON (step ids and paths)
  --apply     roll back

Exit status: 0 done, 1 refusal, or the status of a failed step.
```

## `scan`

Scan files, the staged index or a commit range for secrets and private data.

```text
Usage: dotsteward scan (--tree | --staged | --range RANGE) [OPTION...]

Modes (exactly one):
  --tree           git-visible files of the work tree (tracked and untracked,
                   not ignored); outside git every file below the current
                   directory except .git directories
  --staged         index blobs of the paths staged for the next commit
  --range RANGE    every commit of RANGE (A..B, B, ^A, several separated by
                   spaces): the blobs each commit changed, its message and
                   identities, and annotated tags pointing into the range
Options:
  --metadata          also apply the commit rules (e-mail, UTC dates,
                      forbidden message lines); --range only
  --denylist F        private terms (plain, word:TERM, re:ERE; # comments)
  --require-denylist  refuse to run without a denylist; without --denylist
                      the policy's denylist path is used
  --extra-terms F     more terms in the denylist format
  --redact            print rule and location only, never the matched text
  --secrets-only      only the shape of real credentials, for a tree that is not yours
                      (--tree): no credential assignment in prose, no home path, e-mail,
                      address or non-ASCII rule, no policy file, no denylist
  --instance-policy   the policy of the instance found like every instance
                      command, as `dotsteward static` applies it to personal
                      content: generic secret rules, [privacy] forbidden_paths
                      and file_rules; the terms come from --denylist

The policy is privacy/policy.toml of the scanned repository root when it
exists, otherwise the framework's own; privacy/allowlist.txt next to it
lists public strings that are masked before extra terms are matched. An
allowlist entry that contains a denylist term is refused, unless it is a
commit e-mail address that commits.email accepts. Exit 0 when clean, 1 on
any finding (after collecting all of them) or error.
```

## `settings`

Sync tracked application settings with the instance's settings buffer.

```text
usage: local-maintained-files [-h] [--repo REPO] [--home HOME]
                              [--state-dir STATE_DIR]
                              [--targets-file TARGETS_FILE]
                              [--inactive-components INACTIVE_COMPONENTS]
                              {status,apply,flush,resolve,reconcile,verify,track,track-file,untrack,validate} ...

positional arguments:

                        files

    resolve             decide a conflict or a local deletion
    reconcile           advance the base to the published values
    verify              check that this machine agrees with the repository
    track               start tracking a key
    track-file          start tracking a whole file
    untrack             stop tracking an entry
    validate            check the buffer without touching any file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --repo REPO           instance checkout (default: the discovered instance)
  --home HOME           home directory of the live files
  --state-dir STATE_DIR
                        machine state (default: <state root>/local-maintained-
                        files)
  --targets-file TARGETS_FILE
                        component settings targets and reload hooks (JSON)
  --inactive-components INACTIVE_COMPONENTS
                        JSON list of components not active here: the entries
                        of their targets wait
```

```text
usage: local-maintained-files track [-h] --id ID --target TARGET (--key KEY |
                                    --key-json KEY_JSON) [--note NOTE]

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --id ID
  --target TARGET
  --key KEY
  --key-json KEY_JSON
  --note NOTE
```

```text
usage: local-maintained-files track-file [-h] --id ID --path PATH
                                         --source SOURCE [--mode MODE]

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --id ID
  --path PATH
  --source SOURCE
  --mode MODE
```

### `settings untrack`

```text
usage: local-maintained-files untrack [-h] id

positional arguments:
  id

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

### `settings validate`

```text
usage: local-maintained-files validate [-h]

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

## `skills`

Track the user's own skills, and report what the instance means for this machine.

```text
usage: dotsteward skills [-h] COMMAND ...

Track the user's own skills, and report what the instance means for this
machine.

positional arguments:
  COMMAND
    effective  what this machine leaves out, and why
    status     what the machine knows about the own skills of the lock
    reconcile  compare the skill roots with what is known, without network
    capture    publish the skills that wait, from a separate worktree
    track      answer the question about a skill: --all, --here, --never or
               --later
    resolve    settle a conflict: the local copy or the repository wins
    diff       the three trees of a skill, to compare them
    forget     take a skill out of the repository, for all machines
    restore    install a skill deleted here from the repository again
    retry      try a skill that was kept back again, now
    hooks      the hooks of skill tracking in the configuration of an agent

options:
  -h, --help   show this help message and exit

Exit status: 0 done, 1 refusal, 2 usage error, 3 a conflict or a question
waits, 4 a privacy stop, 6 no network. `skills hook EVENT --agent AGENT` is
what the agents call, and it always exits 0.
```

### `skills effective`

```text
usage: dotsteward skills effective [-h] [--json]

Prints the machine name, its profile and tags, and what it leaves out:
skip.components, skip.skills and skip.plugins, with one word for each in
reasons (machines: the entry is for other machines; declined:
hosts/<name>.toml says never; deleted: an own skill deleted here). name_taken
lists the skills of the lock that are for other machines while this machine
has a skill of that name.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print one JSON document
```

### `skills status`

```text
usage: dotsteward skills status [-h] [--json]

One line per own skill that is not in sync, what ignore rules leave out of a
copy, links that cannot be copied and what waits. With --json the document
with the state of every own skill.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print one JSON document
```

### `skills reconcile`

```text
usage: dotsteward skills reconcile [-h] [--json] [--full]

Finds new skills and changes of own skills and records them in pending.json.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print pending.json
  --full      digest every own skill, whatever its file times say
```

### `skills capture`

```text
usage: dotsteward skills capture [-h] [--now | --wait] [--name SKILL] [--json]

Publishes what waits in pending.json. The checkout stays as it is.

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
  --now         now; ends at once when nothing waits (default)
  --wait        sleep until the deadline, as one process per machine
  --name SKILL  only this skill; may be repeated
  --json        print the result as one JSON document
```

### `skills track`

```text
usage: dotsteward skills track [-h] [--all | --here | --never | --later]
                               [--own] [--no-capture]
                               SKILL

--all puts the skill into the lock for every machine, --here for this machine
only, --never remembers in the host file of this machine that it stays out.
--later declines nothing: the sessions stop asking, and skills status keeps
listing it. A downloaded skill keeps its upstream pinned; --own tracks your
own copy without one, which also turns a pinned skill into yours. --all or
--here takes an earlier --never back.

positional arguments:
  SKILL

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
  --all         for all machines
  --here        for this machine only
  --never       never on this machine
  --later       not now: declines nothing, the sessions stop asking
  --own         your own copy, without an upstream
  --no-capture  record the answer; the next capture takes it
```

### `skills resolve`

```text
usage: dotsteward skills resolve [-h] (--ours | --theirs) SKILL

--ours publishes the local copy. --theirs backs it up and installs the copy of
the repository.

positional arguments:
  SKILL

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --ours      the local copy wins
  --theirs    the repository wins
```

### `skills diff`

```text
usage: dotsteward skills diff [-h] [--json] SKILL

Names the local copy, the copy on the remote and the one this machine last had
in sync.

positional arguments:
  SKILL

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print one JSON document
```

### `skills forget`

```text
usage: dotsteward skills forget [-h] [--clear] SKILL

Removes the skill from the lock and the repository. A local copy stays, and
nobody asks about it. --clear is for later, once no copy is left: this machine
stops keeping the name out, of forget and of track --never alike, and a new
skill of that name is a new skill.

positional arguments:
  SKILL

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --clear     stop keeping out a name whose copy is gone
```

### `skills restore`

```text
usage: dotsteward skills restore [-h] SKILL

Copies the skill of the remote to the canonical skill root.

positional arguments:
  SKILL

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

### `skills retry`

```text
usage: dotsteward skills retry [-h] SKILL

For a skill that is blocked (dotsteward skills status says why) once the cause
is gone: a refusal of the remote is never tried again by itself.

positional arguments:
  SKILL

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

### `skills hooks`

```text
usage: dotsteward skills hooks [-h] [--agent {claude,codex}]
                               {install,check,remove}

install puts the hooks into the configuration of an agent, or removes them
when [skills] tracking is off; check reports and never fails; remove takes
them out until the next rebuild.

positional arguments:
  {install,check,remove}

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --agent {claude,codex}
                        default: the enabled agents
```

## `state`

Record the state this machine observes on its own state branch, push it, fetch and show the state of every machine.

```text
usage: dotsteward state [-h] SUBCOMMAND ...

The state each machine observes, on the branch state/<name> of the instance
remote.

positional arguments:
  SUBCOMMAND
    record    record the state of this machine on its state branch and push it
    push      send the records of this machine that the remote does not have
    fetch     bring the state branches of every machine
    show      print the recorded state of a machine

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

Exit status: 0 done, 1 refusal, 2 usage error, 4 the record breaks its schema
or the privacy scan found something (nothing was recorded), 6 no network or no
login (the record waits; run it again).
```

### `state record`

```text
usage: dotsteward state record [-h] [--no-push]

Observes this machine (platform, kernel, active generation and its last E2E
run, the enabled components of the intent that apply here, the installed
versions of the packages a deb component installs or follows), holds the
document to schema/state.schema.json and the intent, scans it with the privacy
policy of the instance and commits state.json on refs/heads/state/<name>
without touching the checkout. A record equal to the last one is no commit.
Then it pushes like state push.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --no-push   record on this machine only
```

### `state push`

```text
usage: dotsteward state push [-h] [--take-over]

Pushes state/<name> without force. When the remote branch moved on and its
records come from this machine, the record becomes one commit on its tip; when
they come from another machine, the push stops. [policy] observed_state_push =
false keeps the branch on this machine.

options:
  -h, --help   show this help message and exit
  --take-over  this machine is the reinstall of the machine whose name it has:
               continue the records of its branch
```

### `state fetch`

```text
usage: dotsteward state fetch [-h]

Fetches refs/heads/state/* of the remote to refs/remotes/origin/state/*.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

### `state show`

```text
usage: dotsteward state show [-h] [--json] [NAME]

Prints the recorded state of NAME (default: this machine): the local branch of
this machine, what the last state fetch brought for another. --json prints
{host, this_machine, source, queued, state}.

positional arguments:
  NAME        a machine name

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print one JSON document
```

## `static`

Check the static contracts of an instance or of the framework source.

```text
Usage: dotsteward [--instance DIR] static [--sandbox] [--only CHECK]...

Checks the instance found like every instance command (--instance,
DOTSTEWARD_INSTANCE, then the nearest workstation.toml above the working
directory). Without an instance, inside the framework source, it checks the
framework itself. Every failure of every selected check is reported before
the command exits.

Instance checks, in this order:
  shell          bash -n over every shell file (*.sh, or a sh or bash
                 shebang); a file with a shebang is executable, one without
                 declares "# shellcheck shell="; ShellCheck, when installed,
                 at the version versions.lock.json pins
                 (nix_packages.shellcheck.resolved) and without findings
  bans           shell and Nix files outside tests/ never pipe a download
                 into a shell, force a git push or allow package downgrades
  launcher       .dotsteward/cli.sh equals the framework's template copy
  bootstrap      bootstrap.sh equals the framework's template copy, when the
                 framework ships one
  skills         vendored skills match the skills lock: schema,
                 directories, names, digests, licenses (a skill with a
                 repo-owned sentinel revision is the user's own and needs
                 none), no symbolic links and no framework skills
                 (expected_skill_count, a copy of the number of entries, is
                 ignored); the own plugins of the lock (own_plugins) match
                 agent/plugins the same way
  hosts          every hosts/<name>.toml is valid and named like a machine, and
                 every machines key of the lock and of the plugin tables names
                 known machines (dotsteward host check)
  versions-lock  versions.lock.json: schema_version "1.0"; a policy left in
                 it is read by nothing (a warning)
  policy         workstation.toml [policy]: no persistent agentic updates,
                 native application updates kept
  allowlist      no update allowlist entry (gate.update_allowlist and the
                 committed manifest mirrors) matches the settings buffer
  protected      byte-protected files keep their sha256 ([protected])
  overlays       declared overlay files exist; agent/overlays holds only
                 overlays of framework skills (and its README.md)
  privacy        the privacy scan with the instance policy: generic secret
                 rules, [privacy] forbidden_paths and file_rules, the
                 digest-bound [privacy] exemptions, and the
                 [privacy] denylist outside the sandbox; there, in a git
                 work tree, a vendored file (below skills.vendor_dir, no
                 file rule selects it) whose content an earlier scan found
                 nothing in is answered from <state root>/privacy/
                 scan-cache (content digests under a key of the scanner,
                 its rules, the denylist, the exemptions and the
                 instance root; its path is still scanned), and the clean
                 line counts the answers
  scripts        every [gate] static script exists and is executable; when
                 every selected check passed they run in order from the
                 instance root (shell scripts with bash, other scripts
                 through their shebang) with DOTSTEWARD_INSTANCE_ROOT,
                 DOTSTEWARD_SANDBOX (0 or 1) and DOTSTEWARD_STATIC_HELPER (a
                 file to source that defines fail MESSAGE); the first
                 failing script ends the run with its exit status
Framework checks: shell, bans, command-names (the command-name rule: stub
file names, arguments of require_command and of command -v, and fenced
shell blocks of Markdown files name only catalog commands, the platform
tools of tests/static/allowed-commands.txt and the fixture names), seeds
(modules/components/*/seed.json against schema/seed.schema.json) and
privacy (privacy/policy.toml, no denylist).

Options:
  --sandbox     the context of a Nix check: every file below the root is
                listed (no git) and nothing outside the root is read (no
                denylist). Outside a git work tree the files are listed
                the same way without this option.
  --only CHECK  run only the named checks (repeatable; comma-separated
                names are accepted)

Exit status: 0 when every check passed, 1 on a failed check or a usage
error, otherwise the exit status of the failing instance script.
```

## `sync`

Old name of generate: a warning, then generate with the same arguments (until 2.0.0).

```text
[dotsteward] WARNING: 'dotsteward sync' is the old name of 'dotsteward generate'; the old name stops working in 2.0.0
Usage: dotsteward generate [--nix] [--skill NAME]...

Evaluates the instance's dotstewardMirrors output (`nix eval --json
--no-update-lock-file <instance>#dotstewardMirrors`), writes every mirror
that changed to .dotsteward/<name> byte for byte (atomically), removes
manifest.*.json and stage0.*.env mirrors the evaluation no longer
produces, then runs `dotsteward pins sync` with the same flags against the
fresh mirrors. Untracked, not ignored files other than those mirrors are
refused before any Nix call, because Nix does not see them. Exit codes:
0 ok, 1 refusal or error, else the status of `pins sync`.
```

## `txn`

Prepare, publish and report a maintenance transaction.

```text
Usage: dotsteward [--instance DIR] txn prepare --official-sources-only
                  [--scope update|maintain]
       dotsteward [--instance DIR] txn publish [--scope update|maintain]
                  [--expected-base OID]
       dotsteward [--instance DIR] txn status [--json]

The maintenance transaction: prepare records a base, `dotsteward gate`
proves the candidate tree, publish ships a commit whose tree is the proven
tree. Nothing here builds, activates or commits anything.

prepare
  Runs in the instance clone (top of a git work tree, on instance.branch,
  origin exactly instance.remote). The update scope (default) needs an
  entirely clean clone; the maintain scope lists the changes instead. It
  fetches origin/<branch> (60 s), requires HEAD to equal it in both
  scopes, and records <state>/update/candidate.json (schema_version
  "1.1": prepared_at, base_oid, root, scope, official_sources_only,
  persistent_agentic_updates, native_application_updates). Advisory
  checks become warnings in the output, never refusals: the binary cache
  (gate.cache_url) does not answer, /nix/store has less than
  gate.prepare_warn_free_gib GiB free, gh is not logged in or not
  installed. Output: a "prepared" line, then one JSON line {base_oid,
  root, scope, dirty, warnings}.
  --official-sources-only   required: the transaction takes versions
                            only from official sources

publish
  In order: the clone guards; a clean tree; the base OID (--expected-base,
  else base_oid of candidate.json when it was prepared for this instance,
  else `git merge-base HEAD origin/<branch>`; a clone without
  origin/<branch>, a new instance before its first push, is refused with
  the `git push -u` to run); at least one commit after
  the base, which must be an ancestor of HEAD; the HEAD tree is the tree
  of a passed validation.json, made for the same scope and the same base
  and without a framework override; when the transaction activated a tree on this
  machine (<state>/current/activation.json of rebuild --switch: its tree
  is the HEAD tree, or its revision a commit after the base), that tree
  is the HEAD tree and <state>/update/e2e.json records a passed E2E run
  of it, of the activated generation and of the activated profile, with
  the repository checks (publishing without an activation needs no E2E
  record); the commit subjects (update scope: the last one is exactly
  commit.update_subject; maintain scope: every one after the base is a
  conventional commit); a fresh fetch (60 s, into refs/dotsteward/txn/tip
  and origin/<branch>) finds the remote branch still at the base, else
  exit 3 and nothing is pushed; on a named machine every commit to publish
  gets the line Dotsteward-Machine: <name>, whoever wrote it, with the same
  tree, author and dates; HEAD is pushed to <branch> without force (180 s),
  and a push rejected as no fast-forward is exit 3 as well; a fetch then
  makes sure the remote holds HEAD or a commit after it (another machine
  may push at the same moment). When the first fetch finds the remote
  branch already at HEAD, the commit is already published: nothing is
  pushed and the exit status is 0. Without a network the exit status is 6;
  a push whose answer got lost and that landed is published. `dotsteward
  apply` and `dotsteward upgrade` move their commits onto the new tip after
  an exit 3 and publish again. Finally the canonical
  checkout (canonical_repo of <state>/host-overrides/inventory.json, else
  instance.checkout) is fast-forwarded when it is a clean clone of
  instance.remote on <branch> at the base; any other state is a warning,
  never a failure; a path that is not a git repository, or the publishing
  clone itself, is skipped.
  --scope S                 update (default) or maintain
  --expected-base OID       the base OID

status
  Prints the state directory and the paths and records of candidate.json,
  validation.json and validate.log. Reads only; works in any checkout.
  --json                    one JSON document {schema_version: 1,
                            instance, paths: {state_dir, candidate,
                            validation, log}, candidate, validation}; a
                            record is the file's object, or null when the
                            file is absent or not a JSON object

Exit status: 0 done (already published included), 1 refused or failed,
3 publish only: the remote moved since the base (a race another machine won;
nothing was pushed), 6 publish only: no network (nothing was pushed).
```

## `upgrade`

Bring this machine and the shared lock to the newest stable versions, with one command.

```text
usage: dotsteward upgrade [-h] [--tracked | --all] [--plan] [--retry-held]
                          [--json] [--accept KEY]

Brings this machine and the shared lock to the newest stable versions. Without
a flag a terminal asks what to update; without a terminal it is --tracked.
Exit status: 0 done, 1 a refusal or a failed step, 2 usage error, 3 a decision
or a sudo step waits (review.json), 4 a privacy stop, 6 no network: the
network steps were skipped and the checks ran, 130 interrupted: the next run
finishes. Never: an OS release upgrade, autoremove, a reboot.

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
  --tracked     what the instance tracks, then a read only analysis of
                everything else and one offer
  --all         also apt as a whole, snap, flatpak and the tools of
                [[upgrade.tools]]; no second question
  --plan        say what both modes would do and change nothing
  --retry-held  take back every local hold (<state>/holds.json) first, so the
                held pins move again
  --json        print the report as one JSON document
  --accept KEY  answer in advance: install:PACKAGE, series:kernel=X.Y,
                series:nvidia=N, firmware; all of them need a terminal in the
                end
```

## `version`

Print the framework version, source revision and narHash.

```text
Usage: dotsteward version [--json]
```
